extracted.intended_audience: college/university instructors and curriculum designers (graduate-level program evaluation and service-learning), and educators teaching grant writing
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, implementing, and assessing a graduate-level service-learning grant-writing project in a program evaluation course where students ghost-write foundation proposals for community organizations, with specified milestones, proposal elements, and multi-method assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service should be connected to the curriculum
rubrics_metrics.description: Service-learning project must integrate community service with academic coursework so that the service activity directly relates to course content and learning objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper notes the grant-writing project was connected to the Program Evaluation curriculum and thus met this best-practice characteristic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service should involve a specific action
rubrics_metrics.description: The service component should be a concrete task (not vague volunteering) that produces a tangible product or outcome (e.g., writing a grant proposal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The project involved the specific action of grant writing for community organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: There should be student reflection at the end of the service
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must engage in end-of-project reflection about their experiences and learning from the service activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The course required an end-of-project questionnaire and presentations; the paper reports reflection at the end was provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: There should be ongoing reflection throughout the course
rubrics_metrics.description: Reflection should not be limited to the end — opportunities for ongoing reflection during the project should be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper indicates limited emphasis on ongoing reflection and suggests weekly journals as a remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Students should have a choice in selecting the service
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should be allowed to select which community organization or service activity they will work with, giving them agency and alignment with interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students selected organizations to work with (Deadline 1) though they had to complete the grant individually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Students should receive training in the service area
rubrics_metrics.description: Before engaging in service tasks, students should be trained in relevant skills and knowledge needed to perform effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students received a 16-page document, sample proposals, and a grants office presentation; the paper reports students received training in grant writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Students should be involved for a minimum of 10 hours
rubrics_metrics.description: Service-learning involvement should meet a minimum engagement threshold (10 hours) to ensure meaningful participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All students were involved for substantially more than 10 hours in this project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty should be trained in the use of service-learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructors facilitating service-learning should have prior training or experience in service-learning pedagogy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructor attended workshops in the use of service-learning prior to the course.

rubrics_metrics.name: There should be ongoing communication between faculty and community service-learning partner
rubrics_metrics.description: Regular, ongoing contact between instructor and community partners should be maintained throughout the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper notes limited contact (two times) and recommends increased phone/email/brief meetings to improve this characteristic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment should be conducted to determine if program outcomes were achieved
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects must include assessment methods (quantitative and/or qualitative) to evaluate whether learning and service outcomes were met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This project used a pre-post knowledge test, independent reviewer scoring, and qualitative feedback from students and sponsors.

rubrics_metrics.name: There should be recognition of student contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Students' work should be acknowledged by faculty, community partners, or the institution to validate efforts and learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students were recognized by organizational sponsors, faculty, and peers according to the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer scoring criterion: One-page Summary
rubrics_metrics.description: One-page summary of the proposal is evaluated as a discrete scoring item on the reviewer sheet (10 points max).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the 10-item reviewer scoring sheet; reviewers used a 0-10 scale for this and other sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer scoring criterion: Statement of Problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity and strength of the problem statement are assessed (10 points max).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included on reviewer scoring sheet; scored 0-10 by each of four independent reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer scoring criterion: Project Impact on Problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which the proposed project will address or impact the identified problem (10 points max).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the standardized reviewer scoring instrument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer scoring criterion: Implementation Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality and feasibility of implementation steps, timeline, and actions (10 points max).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated by reviewers using the 0-10 scale; proposals included an implementation plan as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer scoring criterion: Staffing
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequacy and appropriateness of staff/roles proposed to carry out the project (10 points max).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a scoring item on the reviewer sheet (appears twice on the sheet as provided in the paper).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer scoring criterion: Feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall feasibility of the project given resources, context, and plan (10 points max).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored by each reviewer; contributes to total (100 points max).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer scoring criterion: Evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Strength and appropriateness of the proposal's evaluation plan (10 points max).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the rubric and emphasized in course instruction linking program evaluation content to the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer scoring criterion: Budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Completeness and justification of the budget and budget narrative (10 points max).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students submitted budgets (Deadline 4) and budget narratives; reviewers scored the budget as one of ten criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer scoring criterion: Overall Neatness and Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation quality, organization, and clarity of the proposal document (10 points max).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included on the reviewer scoring sheet; reviewers also provided overall strengths, weaknesses, and recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring process and aggregation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of the 10 reviewer items scored 0-10 by four independent reviewers; total points max = 100; overall assigned score is the average of the four independent reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers worked independently and did not discuss scores until after completing scoring sheets; the instructor provided a one-page summary with expected information under each section to standardize review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrater reliability and judge selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Use multiple reviewers from different disciplines and compute interrater reliability (Cronbach's alpha) to assess consistency among raters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This project used four faculty reviewers from different disciplines and calculated Cronbach's alpha = .90 indicating high agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required elements of a foundation proposal (proposal structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals should include cover letter, title page, one-page summary, overview of the organization, problem statement, goal, major objectives, sub-objectives, implementation/ evaluation plans, future funding plans, budget, references, and appendices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students were given a 16-page guide and two successful sample proposals to model; rough draft (Deadline 5) and final proposal (Deadline 6) followed this standard format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project timeline and milestone deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: Seven deadlines across the semester with specific deliverables to ensure progress: organization contact (week 2); organizational overview (week 3); problem/implementation/evaluation/funder selection (week 6); budget and budget narrative (week 9); rough draft with full sections (week 11); completed proposal with attached rough draft (week 13); 10-minute oral presentation (week 14).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines were enforced to ensure progress; oral presentation required coverage of organization, services, amount requested, source, statement of need, implementation and evaluation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge assessment: pre-post 20-item test
rubrics_metrics.description: A 20-item multiple-choice knowledge test on preparing foundation grant proposals administered at course start (pretest) and at the end (posttest) to measure student learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as one of four assessment methods; paper reports significant knowledge gains (pre M=7.17 to post M=16.83).

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative assessment: open-ended questionnaires and framework analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect open-ended feedback from students and organizational sponsors and analyze using the 'framework' approach (familiarization, identifying thematic framework, indexing, charting, mapping) with independent coders and consensus resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two judges independently applied the thematic framework; discrepancies (five) were discussed until consensus (100% agreement). Themes identified included marketable skills, knowledge, community service, workload (students) and organizational resources, real world experience, support (sponsors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Role clarity for student 'ghost writers'
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly define and communicate the student's role as a ghost writer (they produce a proposal for the organization but do not necessarily submit or become staff), including what the role is and is not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper highlights initial confusion among students and recommends explicit articulation of the ghost-writer role at course start.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use actual grant funding outcome as a grading measure
rubrics_metrics.description: The success of obtaining funding should not be used as a grading criterion since submission/modification/submission decisions are under the organization's control rather than the student's.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper explicitly argues funding outcome is out of student control and should not determine grades.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workload considerations and recommendation for group projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge and assess the time burden of an individual grant-writing project; consider using partner/group formats (especially in rural areas with fewer community partners) to distribute workload.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students reported high workload; half recommended partner/group formats. Instructor should weigh time demands when grading and structuring the assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor-community partner contact frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain adequate direct contact between instructor and community sponsors beyond initial and final meetings to support project coordination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper notes only two instructor contacts occurred and recommends more frequent contact (calls, emails, meetings) to strengthen partnerships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide students with models and preparatory materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply students with instructional documents (e.g., 'how to prepare grants for foundations'), successful sample proposals, and external presentations (university grants office) to scaffold proposal development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course provided a 16-page guide, two successful proposals, and a grants office presentation as training resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer qualitative feedback: strengths, weaknesses, recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to numeric scores, reviewers should provide narrative comments on overall strengths, overall weaknesses, and recommendations for each proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer scoring sheet included fields for overall strengths, overall weaknesses, and recommendations to give formative feedback.
